newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's ANZ eyes more gains after strong half.
newsitem.headline: Australia's ANZ eyes more gains after strong half.

text.p: Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) chalked up solid profit growth in the six months to March 31 and on Wednesday tipped more gains from lower costs and greater fee income.
"We see our core costs reducing in the second half quite significantly," the bank's chief executive, Don Mercer told a news conference in Sydney.
ANZ reported a net half profit of A$615 million (US$470 million), 18 percent higher than the previous first half of A$520 million and hiked its half dividend to 22 cents from 18 cents.
The bank's stock climbed 18 cents to A$8.75 and touched an all-time record high of A$8.77 after the result as investors factored in the earnings growth and positive outlook.
ANZ's Australian operation was the powerhouse performer, contributing A$405 million to the overall result, a 35 percent rise on the previous first half.
In a statement accompanying the bank's accounts, Mercer said the benefits of the bank's recent Australian restructure programme had flowed through to bottom line earnings.

"The change to our Australian business flowing from the major initiatives is increasingly apparent," he said, noting the increased use of telephone banking and expansion of electronic teller and payments systems.

Analysts said although the Australian unit's results were very good, the figures were bolstered by the treatment of restructuring costs as an abnormal item and a historically low provision for doubtful debts.
ANZ's provision for doubtful debts fell to A$75 million from A$102 million in the previous first half.

The bank booked an after tax abnormal loss of A$96 million for restructuring costs. This was partly offset by a payment of A$65 million in interest by National Housing Bank of India following settlement of a long-running dispute.
"The accounting treatment for that (restructuring costs) for all the banks is a little bit questionable," a Sydney-based bank analyst told Reuters.
Analysts had estimated a net profit of between A$580 million and A$630 million and a dividend of between 19 to 24 cents.
Mike Pulman, bank analyst at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett said the banks's underlying result was better than he had expected.
"Clearly we will be upgrading our numbers for the full year following this result," Pulman said.
ANZ chief financial officer David Craig told the news confererence it would be difficult for the bank's Australian operation to repeat first half growth.
"It would be very tough to say 30 percent in the second half," Craig said.
Craig added pre-emptive mortgage rate cuts earlier in the year would have taken about 10 basis points off the bank's interest margin of 3.1 percent as at March 31.
ANZ's New Zealand earnings rose 13 percent to A$77 million from A$68 million in the first half of 1995/96 while international earnings rose nine percent to A$164 million.
"In New Zealand, underlying earnings remained stable, with net provision releases and a lower effective tax rate leading to a moderate increase in after tax profit," Mercer said.
The bank's international business continued to achieve good growth but a change in the geographic mix of earnings had led to a higher effective tax rate, Mercer said.
ANZ said Mercer, the bank's chief executive for the past five years, would retire later this year.
Mercer's last major task would be implement a program of performance improvement which included a new management structure, the bank said.
